title: The Markandeya Purana
author: vyasa
attributionNote: Ascribed to Vyasa and narrated by the sage Markandeya. Its later chapters, the Devi Mahatmya, are among the earliest Sanskrit scriptures of the Goddess.
description: The Markandeya Purana opens with questions about the duties of the four stages of life and the trouble of a childless king, and moves through cosmology, the ages of the world and the genealogies, closing with the Devi Mahatmya: the Goddess's victory over Madhu and Kaitabha, over Mahishasura and over Shumbha and Nishumbha, recited wherever Durga is worshipped.
historicalContext: The Devi Mahatmya, its chapters 78 to 90, is recited in full at the autumn festival of Navaratri and is the foundational text of Shakta devotion. The Purana's frame narrative and its treatment of ethics and rebirth were also drawn on by later compendia.
availabilityNote: Complete: the Sanskrit text of chapters 1 to 93 as GRETIL publishes it, streamed from GRETIL at read time, one chapter at a time. This is the original Sanskrit, not a translation.
